Hi Tom — great to meet you and thanks for the clear targets. Quick recap and proposed next steps below. Looping in Vivek (inference lead) and Rishi (solutions/CS) to scope the eval run.

Recap / recommendations:
- Baseline models: Llama-3-16B and RedSea-13B (lossy-resistant gen). Run both as FP16 baselines.
- Quantization candidates to test (order): AWQ (8-bit asymmetric), GPTQ (4/8-bit post-training), FP8 (hardware-accelerated where available).
- Tradeoff expectations: AWQ typically gives ~2-2.5x throughput with minimal short-answer drift; GPTQ (4-bit) gives highest size reduction but requires careful per-layer tuning and may show more degradation on long-context coherence; FP8 (on supported GPUs) gives larger perf gain with modest quality change but is hardware-dependent.

Proposed deliverables for a 10-business-day trade study:
1) Baseline run (FP16) on your 500-prompt set + key traces — metrics: accuracy/ROUGE, BLEU, hallucination flags, latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens.
2) AWQ 8-bit run + compare.
3) GPTQ 4-bit exploratory run (spot-check subsets, 50 prompts) + quality regression report.
4) FP8 run on supported infra (if you provide Dedicated cluster or we can run on Redwood Hosted dedicated pool).
5) Recommendation matrix + CSV benchmarks + short deck.

Attachments I prepared: finwave_prompt_set.txt (placeholder for upload), quant_trade_study_awq_v_gptq_fp8.pdf (high-level tradeoffs), model_benchmarks.csv (example outputs). Links to our benchmark runner and prior case studies included below.

- Any red flags in the prompt set re: PII or privacy controls? If so, please flag before upload.

- If you want deeper 4-bit GPTQ tuning, add another 3–5 business days.

Tom — happy to set up a quick sync tomorrow to align on timeline.

Best,

Adding a few engineering specifics so expectations are clear. Picking the right quantization path is workload-dependent; below are patterns we've seen and recommended config presets for the trade study.

AWQ (8-bit asymmetric):
- Pros: fast to apply, stable across generative tasks, good end-to-end throughput uplift (~2x) without major per-layer tuning.
- Cons: slightly denser model file vs 4-bit; edge-case regressions on rare-token distributions.
- Preset: AWQ-8 + mild per-head clipping + KV cache preservation.

GPTQ (4-bit):
- Pros: best model size reduction and cost savings, large throughput gains if model fits cache and kernels optimized.
- Cons: higher risk of long-form degradation and hallucination; requires layer-wise reconstruction and eval.
- Preset: GPTQ-4 with per-layer lr-sweep, selective dequantization for attention layers. Run on subset first (50–100 prompts).

FP8 (hardware-dependent):
- Pros: near FP16 quality on many tasks, very high throughput on Ampere+ or newer GPUs with Tensor Cores supporting FP8.
- Cons: limited availability in some Dedicated clusters; requires kernel support.
- Preset: FP8-e4m3 where supported; compare against AWQ baseline.

Quality regression notes (what we monitor):
- Multi-step coherence (long summaries), entity hallucination counts, generation length distribution shifts, top-1/top-5 token probability anomalies.
- We will run ranking/metrics and also produce spot-checks with reference outputs and human review snippets for any flagged regressions.

Benchmark plan and timeline (concrete):
- Day 0: confirm prompt set + infra preference.
- Days 1–2: baseline FP16 run (500 prompts) + initial metrics.
- Days 3–5: AWQ runs across both models + full metrics and CSV export.
- Days 6–8: GPTQ exploratory (subset) + regression report.
- Day 9–10: FP8 run (if infra available) + final recommendation deck.

I attached the trade study PDF and the sample benchmarks CSV. If FinWave wants us to run on their Dedicated cluster, we need a short onboarding window for agent access and GPU topology; otherwise we can run on Redwood Dedicated (same configs) and share raw logs.

-Vivek
